title: What are Ensemble Methods?
description: How combining multiple models through bagging and boosting yields more robust predictions than any single model.
content:
**Ensemble methods** involve combining several models to improve predictive performance over any single model. They leverage the crowd wisdom phenomenon, generally ensuring more robust performance.

The two core approaches to building ensembles:
• Bagging
• Boosting

**Bagging** is an ensemble method that involves independent training of the same learning algorithm on different subsets of the training data (i.e., implementing data bootstrap). Bagging helps to reduce variance and overfitting, ensuring more robust solutions for problems.

**Boosting** is an ensemble method that focuses on sequential training of the same learning algorithm, where each subsequent model corrects the errors of its ancestor. The training process assigns higher weights to misclassified instances, prioritizing them in subsequent iterations.

Common examples of ensembles:
• Random forest - combines multiple decision trees and aggregates their predictions to make the final prediction.
• Gradient boosting machines (GBM) - build models sequentially by fitting a new model to the residual errors of the previous model; essentially, they use gradient descent in function space to minimize a total loss function.
• Voting models - combine multiple classification or regression models and aggregate their predictions (majority voting for classification, averaging for regression) to make the final prediction.
